title: Para-Gaussian vs Gaussian approximation of random-network preactivations
setting: Randomly initialized fully connected networks (standard Gaussian weights, 1/sqrt(n) scaling, unit-variance input, linear or normalized ReLU sqrt(2)·max(0,x)) of width n and depth L; 4000 random networks are sampled, and the layer-L neuron's law is the exact conditional-Gaussian mixture over the sampled random covariance. Predictors are N(0,1) or the para-Gaussian density φ(x)[1+κ4/4!·He4(x)] with κ4=3[(1+c/n)^L−1] (c=2 linear, c=5 ReLU). The metric is the binned (width 0.1) total variation distance between the predictor and the Monte Carlo law.

paper.title: Para-Gaussian Approximations of Random Deep Neural Networks
paper.claim: A para-Gaussian (Gaussian plus fourth-cumulant Hermite correction) approximation matches the finite-width distribution of random network preactivations better than the Gaussian approximation, and the gap matters most at small width and large depth.

metric.name: tv_binned
metric.description: Binned total variation distance (bin width 0.1 on [-8,8] plus two tail bins) between the approximating distribution and the Monte Carlo distribution of a layer-L preactivation. Lower is better.

factors.name: method
factors.description: Approximating law: infinite-width Gaussian N(0,1); para-Gaussian with Hermite He4 correction (signed density); or para-Gaussian with negative bin masses clipped to zero and renormalized.

factors.name: width
factors.description: Hidden layer width n; non-Gaussian corrections scale like 1/n.

factors.name: depth
factors.description: Number of weight layers L at which the preactivation is measured; non-Gaussianity compounds with depth, possibly beyond where a first-order correction is valid.

factors.name: activation
factors.description: Nonlinearity: identity (exactly solvable) or normalized ReLU (approximate recursion).
